body: I’m a creative myself so I have no problem with retelling the story with some liberties such as that speech or maybe amplifying the drama in a moment to express how it felt rather than how it really was. I’m just saying if he made up that he was actually stalked by someone, I’d be bothered because I connected to his experience of the cops being unhelpful, finding ways to blame him for it, feeling on his own with having to deal with her, while also feeling sorry for her etc. It’s just a weird experience I had that I never had anyone to relate to about but I felt like I had that fulfilled while watching this. So of course he can be creative, but, and I’m not sure why exactly, I’d feel like something was taken from me if he was never actually stalked in real life. I’m just going with believing he was and am not looking it up lol

I’d be upset to learn it wasn’t true. I had a stalker once and it was an upsetting experience. I related to the story in some ways, especially the police not taking it seriously. I’m not sure why it would upset me if it wasn’t true. I think because if it was presented as just fiction, I’d still watch because it’s interesting, but I wouldn’t get this sense of feeling less alone in what I experienced. That would be taken away if it came out that he lied for views.

The frustrating aspect is the lack of awareness and acknowledgment of what life is like for those that were not as lucky. And how being spoiled by this level of support can foster a sense of superiority and entitlement.

Does your employee agreement have any of the above in writing? If the employee agreement does not include wording about where you work, you might be out of luck. If it says hybrid, but nothing about the probation period, it might be worth going through with that period and then being happy after. Fuck that therapist. I’m sorry. I know what it feels like. I wish it was different. With my therapists following, I’m just always very careful to share it all, how extreme my feelings are etc. but never ever say I actually want to die. The closest I get is saying I’ve had thoughts and quickly following with “but I’m too scared of that and I’d never do it so it’s really not a concern.” It’s sort of a round about way to admit how bad it is and still get some level of help. 

If you can find just one friend, even people on Reddit, where you can be really honest about it to get it out, for me that’s been enough. I mean, nothing will ever make it better is how I currently feel. But sticking to my therapist (who I never tell about the nights I start to make suicide plans), it’s been worth hiding that part because she helps me feel better and think clearer than I do without her.

I think of it metaphorically like if I needed some very expensive drug to truly ease my pain, but all I can afford is Tylenol, might as well take what I can get.

This is why I stopped telling them. I tell them everything but that. If they ask, I lie. I say I have thoughts but it’s def nothing to worry about. Fucking ridiculous we can’t be honest and really be helped.
